meta.title: Icelandic Alphabet
meta.subtitle: The 32 letters and their sounds, then diphthongs, stress and length (39 notes) · both directions, as two cards each
meta.desc: The Icelandic alphabet and its sounds: 39 notes — the thirty-two letters in Icelandic alphabetical order, capital and small, with each one's Icelandic name; then seven notes on what no single letter shows: the diphthongs ei/ey and au, hv, ll, the breath before a doubled p, t or k, the stress, and vowel length. The first deck of the Icelandic collection. Icelandic uses the Latin alphabet with letters English does not have — þ and ð, the two "th" sounds of thin and this; æ, the i of ice; ö — and an accented partner for six vowels that is a letter of its own with a sound of its own (á is the "ow" of cow, é the "ye" of yes); it has no c, q, w or z. Both directions: see a letter and recall its sound, or see a sound and recall the letter, each a card with its own schedule. Every note describes the sound in English words and gives one word that shows it, with a speaker beside the letter and the word. The sounds are approximations, as every learner's alphabet gives them; where English has no equivalent — u, ö, au — the card says what to do instead. Sources: the standard description of Icelandic spelling and pronunciation; the example words are checked against English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0).

fields.Name: a
fields.Sound: "a" as in father — held long in a stressed syllable before one consonant

fields.Name: á
fields.Sound: "ow" as in cow — a letter of its own, not a kind of a

fields.Name: bé
fields.Sound: "p" as in spin, without a puff of breath — never the full buzz of English b

fields.Name: dé
fields.Sound: "t" as in stop, without a puff of breath

fields.Name: eð
fields.Sound: "th" as in this — never at the start of a word

fields.Name: e
fields.Sound: "e" as in bed

fields.Name: é
fields.Sound: "ye" as in yes

fields.Name: eff
fields.Sound: "f" as in fun at the start of a word; "v" between vowels and at the end of a word (hafa, "to have"); "p" before l or n (nafn, "name")

fields.Name: ge
fields.Sound: "k" as in skin, without a puff of breath, at the start of a word; between vowels it softens to a breathy sound made at the back of the mouth (saga, "story")

fields.Name: há
fields.Sound: "h" as in hat — and hv is said "kv" (hvað, "what")

fields.Name: i
fields.Sound: "i" as in sit

fields.Name: í
fields.Sound: "ee" as in see

fields.Name: joð
fields.Sound: "y" as in yes — never the j of jam

fields.Name: ká
fields.Sound: "k" as in kit, with a puff of breath at the start of a word; "ky" before e, i, í, y, ý, æ and ei (kind, "sheep")

fields.Name: ell
fields.Sound: "l" as in leaf — and ll is said like "tl" (fjall, "mountain")

fields.Name: emm
fields.Sound: "m" as in man

fields.Name: enn
fields.Sound: "n" as in net — and nn after an accented vowel or a diphthong is said like "tn" (steinn, "stone")

fields.Name: o
fields.Sound: "o" as in British hot, the lips rounded

fields.Name: ó
fields.Sound: "o" as in go, gliding to "oo" — never the o of hot

fields.Name: pé
fields.Sound: "p" as in pen, with a puff of breath at the start of a word

fields.Name: err
fields.Sound: a rolled or tapped "r", as in Scottish English — always said, wherever it stands

fields.Name: ess
fields.Sound: "s" as in see — never a z sound

fields.Name: té
fields.Sound: "t" as in top, with a puff of breath at the start of a word

fields.Name: u
fields.Sound: no English sound: the German ü of hübsch — say "i" as in sit with the lips rounded

fields.Name: ú
fields.Sound: "oo" as in food

fields.Name: vaff
fields.Sound: "v" as in van

fields.Name: ex
fields.Sound: "ks" as in box

fields.Name: ufsilon i
fields.Sound: the same sound as i, "i" as in sit — the two letters are spelt apart for history, not sound

fields.Name: ufsilon í
fields.Sound: the same sound as í, "ee" as in see — spelt apart from í for history, not sound

fields.Name: þorn
fields.Sound: "th" as in thin — met only at the start of a word

fields.Name: æ
fields.Sound: "eye" — the i of ice

fields.Name: ö
fields.Sound: the German ö or the French eu: say "e" as in bed with the lips rounded

fields.Name: tvíhljóð ei
fields.Sound: both spellings are one sound, "ay" as in day

fields.Name: tvíhljóð au
fields.Sound: no English sound: ö gliding into í, the lips rounded at the start — never the "aw" of English

fields.Name: hv
fields.Sound: said "kv", the k with a puff of breath

fields.Name: tvöfalt l
fields.Sound: said "tl", the tongue held for the l (fjall "mountain", allur "all")

fields.Name: aðblástur
fields.Sound: a doubled p, t or k is said with a puff of breath BEFORE it, like an h: takk is said "tahk"

fields.Name: áhersla
fields.Sound: the stress: every word is stressed on its FIRST syllable, whatever its length

fields.Name: lengd
fields.Sound: a vowel is LONG in a stressed syllable before one consonant or none, and short before two: matur "food" (long a), takk "thanks" (short a)
